current_evidence: The council's 'Guides to planning applications' page links only to this document ('View the local validation list'), says the requirements apply to applications submitted from 1 April 2020, and a search found no newer list or consultation; the document itself says its content is still the 2020 list, reformatted for accessibility.

issues.detail: The List date 2024-02-01 comes from the PDF's CreationDate metadata. The document text says it is the 2020 list reformatted, with requirements in force from 1 April 2020. The date should be 2020-04-01, with consultation running from Nov 2019 to Jan 2020. The 'Outdated (>2y)' flag is right, but the date behind it is not.
issues.evidence: "This document has been reformatted to ensure it is accessible. The content is still as per the 2020 published validation list with some corrected links"; "The Local Requirements within this List come into effect on the 1 April 2020"

issues.detail: Air Quality Impact Assessment is not captured. Trigger: development that may increase air pollution (significant traffic or parking increases, dust) or puts sensitive uses in areas of poor air quality.
issues.evidence: Local List heading 'Air Quality Impact Assessment'

issues.detail: Flood Risk Assessment is not captured as a requirement. Only a fragment about the Sequential/Exception Test appears. Trigger: development in Flood Zone 2 or 3 (including minor development and change of use), sites over 1ha in Zone 1, smaller Zone 1 sites with more vulnerable uses or other flood sources, and areas with critical drainage problems.
issues.evidence: 'Flood Risk Assessment' - "In flood zone 2 or 3 including minor development and change of use"

issues.detail: Land Contamination Assessment is not captured. Trigger: known or suspected contamination, sensitive uses (e.g. residential or educational), or sites within 250m of a former landfill or other potentially contaminated land.

Noise and Vibration Impact Assessment is not captured. Trigger: noise-generating development near noise-sensitive uses or the reverse, mixed-use schemes combining both, and noise-generating uses near wildlife or tranquil areas.
issues.evidence: Local List heading 'Noise and Vibration Impact Assessment'

issues.detail: Energy / Sustainability Assessment is not captured. Trigger: new-build commercial schemes of 1,000 sq m or more, residential sites of 0.5ha or more or 10+ dwellings, conversions to residential, and large non-residential extensions or conversions. Its waste and recycling provision part applies to all applications.

Several other local requirements are missing: Planning Statement (all major development); Economic Statement (new employment uses, or loss of existing B-class employment uses); Minerals Impact Assessment (development affecting safeguarded mineral deposits, or within 250m of or causing loss of a safeguarded minerals facility); Structural Survey (substantial demolition, doubtful structural stability of a building to be converted, or demolition/structural works affecting listed buildings, conservation areas or heritage assets); Telecommunications Development Statement (all telecommunications applications).
issues.evidence: Local List headings 'Planning Statement', 'Economic Statement', 'Minerals Impact Assessment', 'Structural Survey', 'Telecommunications Development Statement'

issues.detail: Some application types are shown as '(none)' even though the list has drawing requirements specific to them. Advertisement consent: the list has 'Advertisement consent drawings' for all express consent applications. Variation of condition s73 and Non-material amendment: the list has 'Drawings relating to Amendment Applications' for s73 and s96a applications. Listed building consent: the list has '4. Listed Building Consent and Certificates' drawings for most alterations to a listed building, but Grokbot captured only Lighting. '1c. Sections' (new or altered buildings, changes in ground level, sloping sites, roof-level accommodation) is also missing.
issues.evidence: "This applies to all Applications for Express Consent."; "This is applicable to Minor Material (section 73) Amendments or Non-material Amendments (section 96a)."; "This is required for most alterations to a listed building."

issues.detail: Lighting Assessment is placed under Listed building consent only because the trigger text mentions 'listed buildings'. The source applies it to any development with external or flood lighting in public places, near homes, listed buildings or conservation areas, near wildlife sites, in open countryside, or next to a highway. It is not an LBC-specific requirement.
issues.evidence: "Where external lighting or floodlighting is provided or made necessary by development in: a publicly accessible location the vicinity of residential property, listed buildings or conservation areas..."

issues.detail: About 19 requirements carry the note 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', but the source often limits them further or applies them more widely. For example, Daylight/Sunlight is for Major development only; Viability is for major residential development, loss of a pub, or harm to heritage assets; site levels apply to 'any extensions or new buildings', which includes householder schemes. 'Roof plan' is placed under Householder only, but '1b. Floor Plans' applies to all applications involving building works; 'householder' appears only in a scale note.
issues.evidence: "This applies to applications for Major development" (Daylight/Sunlight); 1b Floor Plans: "Applications that involve building works (including changes of use)"

issues.detail: Daylight / Sunlight / Overshadowing: Grokbot's trigger 'All submissions must include an overshadowing study' leaves out the threshold. The source applies only to Major development where daylight or sunlight could be adversely affected.
issues.evidence: "This applies to applications for Major development: where there is a potential adverse impact upon the current levels of sunlight and daylight"

issues.detail: Ecological Survey: the trigger is a garbled, incomplete fragment ('A PEA is usually required and for small scale developments...'). The real trigger is Major development and other development likely to affect designated sites, protected species or habitats, with bat surveys where buildings or roofs are affected. 'Biodiversity Net Gain' is a separate row whose trigger is just 'to demonstrate a Biodiversity Net Gain.' It is a clause inside the 2020 Biodiversity Survey requirement, not a standalone local requirement.
issues.evidence: "This applies to applications for Major development and other development likely to have a biodiversity impact on..."

issues.detail: The Arboricultural Impact Assessment / Tree Survey trigger excerpt is actually the text of the Utilities/Drainage requirement ('For applications of major developments & minor developments which will increase site coverage...'). The real 'Tree Survey & Report' trigger is development affecting trees on or adjoining the site, or works to trees.

Several triggers are content or process fragments, not when-required text. Viability: the excerpt is about a solicitor's undertaking for review costs; the real triggers are major residential, other major development, loss of a public house, demolition of or harm to a heritage asset, and existing-use viability. Retail Impact: the excerpt is a change-of-use fragment; the real trigger is retail or leisure over 2,499 sq m outside defined centres, or proposals not in line with the Local Plan. Planning Obligations: the excerpt 'The Statement must be linked to...' comes from another section; the real trigger is where planning obligations are proposed. Ventilation: the A3/A4/A5 use-class trigger is missing.
issues.evidence: Viability: "Major residential development... Any application proposing the loss of a public house"; Ventilation: "Development within Use Classes A3, A4, and A5 or where retail, business, industrial, commercial..."

issues.detail: Some rows are parts of other requirements, not separate local requirements. 'Archaeological Assessment / Desk-based Assessment' is a clause of the Heritage Statement. 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' is part of the Flood Risk Assessment. 'Highways / access details (visibility splays)' and 'Waste / Refuse storage' ('location of waste storage') are fragments of the block plan drawing standards. Transport Assessment and Travel Plan repeat the same cut-off excerpt.
issues.evidence: Heritage Statement: "in the case of archaeological assets, the provision of a desk-based assessment and, where necessary..."

issues.detail: Tab items include boilerplate and broken fragments. 'Setting out the information requirements in a local checklist helps to ensure...' is introductory text. 'where special circumstances form part of the justification...' is general guidance. 'be included for all elevations affected...' and 'show the proposed building including each floor... show internal storage and' are drawing-standard fragments cut off mid-sentence. 'Design and Access Statement' and 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' use content guidance or national (Part 1) text, not local triggers.
issues.evidence: tab_items sections 'Local forms / checklists' and 'Submission rules'

summary: Grokbot's link is the council's only and current local list. Its date is wrong: it comes from PDF metadata, while the text says this is the 2020 list in force from 1 April 2020. The extraction misses many local requirements (Air Quality, Flood Risk Assessment, Contamination, Noise, Energy, Planning Statement and others) and the drawing requirements for adverts, amendments and LBC, and many of its triggers are garbled fragments or attached to the wrong application type.
